pr_title: Bluetooth: Audio: Dereference null return value in cap_initiator.c
pr_body:
Null pointer dereferences in functions:
  bt_cap_initiator_unicast_audio_update (Line 1478)
  bt_cap_initiator_unicast_audio_stop (Line 1693)

Fixes https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/74729
Fixes https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/74739

The 2 CAP initiator issue makes sense to have in the same PR, but please do create separate PRs for unrelated changes (such as https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/74733).

review_comments: Does this indicate some stack-internal bug, or can this happen if the app passes something invalid to this API? Just trying to understand if `CHECKIF()` would be more appropriate than an assert.
Do we have guidelines on that?
But it was checked before in the `valid_unicast_audio_stop_param` function. Isn't that enough?

> Does this indicate some stack-internal bug,

It does indicate a stack-internal bug. The `valid_unicast_audio_update_param` check above prevent `proc_param` from ever being NULL.

True. As mentioned in previous comments, at line 1478, the `proc_param` was checked in `valid_unicast_audio_update_param` to prevent it from being null. Similarly, at line 1995, it was checked in `valid_unicast_audio_stop_param`.
Hmm, @jhedberg maybe you know, but actually IIRC coverity (at least in the past) has not run with asserts enabled. In which case, adding an `__assert` won't make coverity happy here either.

In lines 929, 1132, 1231, and 1313 (of `cap_initiator.c`), it is handled in the same way (by `__ASSERT` after `get_next_proc_param`). So, if this approach is not acceptable, then all should be changed.

> In lines 929, 1132, 1231, and 1313 (of `cap_initiator.c`), it is handled in the same way (by `__ASSERT` after `get_next_proc_param`). So, if this approach is not acceptable, then all should be changed.

That's a good point. Let's assume coverity will accept it :) If we want to apply a different check than an assert, we should do that, but for all. That's outside the scope of this PR though IMO (and something that's currently being discussed in https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/73316
